references.text: A similar introductory formula where the Lord speaks to Moses, introducing the laws about leprosy that Leviticus 14 continues to address.
The same introductory formula is used later in the same chapter when the Lord gives Moses further instructions about leprosy in houses.
The Lord speaking to Moses as a recurring pattern throughout the books of Moses, establishing Moses as the mediator of God's law to Israel.
A parallel text on how lepers were to be handled in the camp, complementing the cleansing rituals in Leviticus 14.
The basic introductory formula for the entire book of Leviticus, where the Lord calls out to Moses and speaks to him.
